subject: GCP private offer — dual-region commitment & CFO signoff
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@orbit-analytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Thu, 10 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: GCP private offer — draft & ask for CFO signoff timeline

Alex — following up from our call yesterday. Attached is the initial private-offer draft for Orbit (GCP) that reflects the commercial points we discussed. High-level proposal:

- Term: 18 months (preferred start: 2028-06-01)
- Committed monthly vGPU-hours: 1,000 (baseline across two regions)
- Regions: us-east1 (70% of usage) / europe-west1 (30% of usage) — customer requested split for latency and data residency
- Billing: we can either issue a single PO that Redwood invoices and applies regional tax/proration, or create two region-specific private offers so Orbit can place two POs (one for US consumption, one for EU) — see note below
- Ramp: 6-month staged acceptance window with capped burst for months 1–3 (up to 30% over commit)

Action items / asks from Orbit for a clean procurement path:
1) Confirm whether procurement requires two separate POs (US/EU) or prefers a single PO with a regional breakdown on invoices.
2) CFO approval expected (we should aim for signoff by 2028-05-20 to keep the 6/1 start).
3) Procurement will likely ask for SOC2 attestation and a short security intake (we've attached our SOC2 PDF).

Attachments: GCP_Private_Offer_Draft_20280510.pdf, MAA_Signoff_Checklist.xlsx

If splitting into two private offers is preferred, Redwood can coordinate with GCP marketplace team to create parallel private-offer records — that avoids complicated cross-border invoicing on Orbit's side. Ben / Kimberly — added you for capacity/billing and legal redline awareness.

Thanks,

Marissa
Sr. Account Exec | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@orbit-analytics.com>

Cc: procurement@orbit-analytics.com
Date: Fri, 11 May 2028 15:34:00 +0100
Subject: Re: GCP private offer — draft & ask for CFO signoff timeline

Thanks Marissa — received and reviewed at a high level. A few clarifying points from procurement / finance: 

- Orbit prefers two POs if possible (one for Orbit, Inc. US entity; one for Orbit Ltd. EU entity) — this simplifies our VAT reclaim and local ledger. Does Redwood have experience issuing two marketplace private offers for the same deal?
- We need SOC2 TYPE II and a short completed security intake questionnaire (I attached our standard procurement form).
- Can you confirm how taxes will be handled for EU usage if Redwood invoices from the US entity?
- Our CFO also wants a staging approach — approve a 6-month ramp with a monthly true-up vs. upfront annual prepayment. Is Redwood comfortable with monthly invoicing against committed usage and a quarterly reconciliation?

Procurement attaching: Orbit_Procurement_Form.xlsx

Proposed next step: quick alignment call with CFO + procurement + Redwood (we're available Tue 18 May 10:00 BST).

—Alex
VP, Finance & Ops | Orbit Analytics
alex.turner@orbit-analytics.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@orbit-analytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Sat, 12 May 2028 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: GCP private offer — draft & ask for CFO signoff timeline

Alex — great questions, answers inline below.

> Orbit prefers two POs if possible. Does Redwood have experience issuing two marketplace private offers for the same deal?
Yes — we can coordinate with GCP marketplace to issue two linked private offers. Each private offer can be bound to the corresponding legal entity and respective tax jurisdiction; usage attribution will be split by region as requested (70/30). Operationally that is the cleanest for your accounting team.

> Need SOC2 TYPE II and security intake questionnaire
Attached: Redwood_SOC2_Report_2028.pdf. We'll also complete a redacted security intake; Ben will own the questionnaire response.

> How are taxes handled for EU usage if Redwood invoices from the US entity?
If you accept two private offers and Orbit EU is the contracting party for the EU PO, Redwood will invoice Orbit EU directly for the EU private offer, which avoids VAT cross-charging. If you choose a single global PO, our billing team will apply regional VAT rules but it is more complex on your side for reclaim.

> Monthly invoicing and quarterly reconciliation?
We can do monthly invoicing against committed usage with quarterly reconciliation and an end-of-term true-up. For the initial 3 months we can permit capped burst (up to +30%) as a ramp buffer; excess above that will be billed at pay-as-you-go rates unless you move to a higher committed band.

Proposed timeline:
- May 17: Redwood legal sends a short redline packet (minor indemnity & data residency language)
- May 18: Alignment call with CFO/procurement (your proposed slot)
- May 20: Target CFO signoff / PO issuance window

I've uploaded a DocuSign preview for the PO language here: https://docusign.com/prepare/0a1b2c3d (preview only).

Ben — I'll need the SOC2 intake answers and a final note on burst billing cap. Kimberly — please prepare a concise redline summary (one page) we can send to Orbit legal ahead of Tue's call.

Thanks — Marissa

Subject: Re: GCP private offer — legal redlines & next steps

Marissa / Alex — I reviewed the draft and prepared a short redline summary. High-level points for Orbit legal to note: 

1) Indemnity: Redwood requests mutual indemnification language; suggested compromise keeps customer data indemnity carveouts standard and limits Redwood's exposure to direct damages capped at the amount paid in the 12 months prior to claim.
2) Data residency: we will include the region mapping clause (us-east1 / europe-west1) and a logging/audit clause for requests that access EU-subject data.
3) SLA & remedies: standard SLA with service credits; we cannot accept termination-for-convenience in the initial committed term.
4) Export controls: small standard clause; not an issue for Orbit based on current use-case.

Attachments: (1) Redline_Summary_20280513.docx (stub referenced here) — we can post the full redline to the shared Drive if Orbit prefers collaboration on tracked changes.

If Orbit legal can confirm accepts our indemnity cap language (or propose changes prior to Tue call), we can expedite the DocuSign flow.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.inference.com
